title: Pi as an unattended worker: verify it live and give it a real full-auto template
description:
Pi is reachable as a herdr kind but is NOT verified for unattended work, so any
role routed to it starts without a full-auto template and can stall on a
permission prompt. Pi supports unattended operation; nobody has established HOW
under herdr, and the kinds table says so honestly rather than guessing.

Verified 2026-09-10 by exercising the real validator (Compile with kind "pi"):

- A provider-qualified Cloudflare id compiles and produces
  `--model cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3:high`. Effort is a SUFFIX
  for pi (effortStyleSuffix), not a flag.
- Every compile emits: `kind "pi" has no verified full-auto template in
  herdr-kinds.md; starting without one.` It is a WARNING, not a refusal, so a
  run starts and may simply hang.
- `internal/herd/config/kinds.go` pi row: fullAuto nil, fullAutoVerified false,
  modelFlag `--model`, effortFlag `--thinking`, efforts off..max, modelOK
  providerQualified. Its comment records that the row was read from `pi --help`
  only.
- Local Pi is 0.85.1. `pi auth check --provider cloudflare-workers-ai` reports
  ready with an api_key, and `pi --list-models` lists 18 cloudflare-workers-ai
  models, so the provider side is genuinely set up.

Do:
1. Find pi's real unattended story from `pi --help` and its docs — the flag or
   config that suppresses approval prompts, whatever it is called. Do not
   transcribe another kind's shape.
2. Round-trip it live, following herdr-kinds.md "Adding a kind" exactly: create
   a WORKSPACE (never `pane split --current`, which resolves to whatever the
   operator is looking at), `herdr agent start` with the candidate template,
   confirm the ECHOED argv, prompt with `--wait`, read the pane for the answer,
   record `herdr agent get` and the `agent_session`.
3. Verify resume: C-c (not `ctrl-c`, which errors `unsupported key`), restart in
   the same pane with a FRESH agent name, confirm the prior turn is present.
4. Record the integration state (`herdr integration status`), since the wave
   loop depends on lifecycle states.
5. Clean up every pane and workspace created.
6. Then set fullAuto and fullAutoVerified in the pi row, and write the pi
   section of herdr-kinds.md from what you actually ran.

Also fix, found alongside:
- `providerQualified` (kinds.go:306) only checks for a slash ANYWHERE, so a bare
  Cloudflare id like `@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3` passes while naming no provider, and
  would reach pi unqualified. Tighten it, or say why the loose check is right.
- Pi's catalog marks which models support thinking. Several cloudflare entries
  do not, and the effort suffix is appended unconditionally, so an economy tier
  on a non-thinking model likely fails at launch. Decide whether that is a
  compile-time refusal (opencode's precedent, kinds.go, treats a missing effort
  dimension as a refusal rather than a silent drop) or a documented constraint.

Placement: the capability matrix is EXECUTION config, so it is ticfac's under
Phase 2 — which is why this tick lives here and not in the ticks tracker. It is
blocked behind the config split (wgi) because the pi row belongs beside the
roles and tiers tables once those are ticfac's. The live round-trip itself can
be done against the current ticks code at any time; what must land here is the
verified template, in ticfac.

Sources to read first, both in the ticks repo today:
`internal/herd/config/kinds.go` (the matrix and its validators) and
`skills/ticks/references/herdr-kinds.md` ("Adding a kind", the green-start trap,
and the operational notes that bit during the opencode round trip).

Two of those notes will bite here: verify the CLI is on the INTERACTIVE shell's
PATH (`zsh -i -c 'which pi'`), because herdr starts the agent in a pane at an
interactive prompt; and `herdr agent prompt --wait` without `--until` matches
idle|done|blocked and does not track turns, so an already-working agent's
current turn can satisfy the wait.

## Specifying WHICH pi model a tier uses, robustly

The mechanism already exists and needs no new syntax: a tier overlay may set
kind, model and effort together, exactly as the `balanced` tier does today for
codex (`.tick/runners.toml`). A pi tier is therefore:

    [roles.implement.tiers.economy]
    kind = "pi"
    model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash"
    effort = "low"

What is NOT robust is everything that decides whether that string means what it
says. Three specific problems, all in scope here:

1. THE SUBSTITUTION QUESTION, which is the whole of robustness. opencode was
   caught silently swallowing an unknown model id: `--model
   openai/gpt-9-imaginary` started green, answered the first-round-trip gate
   with a clean OK, and ran the entire turn on the CLI's own default, with only
   the pane footer betraying it (herdr-kinds.md, observed 2026-08-13). If pi
   does the same, a tier is decorative: the run reports the model it asked for
   and bills a different one. DETERMINE THIS EMPIRICALLY, first, with a
   deliberately bad id. The answer decides how strict the rest must be. Note
   `pi models` reports the session's current model in-band, which may be the
   read-back that catches a substitution.

2. VALIDATE AGAINST PI'S OWN CATALOG, not a regex. `providerQualified`
   (kinds.go:306) only asks whether a slash appears somewhere, so every typo
   passes. pi ships a real oracle: `pi --list-models` prints provider, model,
   context, max-out, THINKING and images (84 rows here), and `pi --list-models
   <search>` filters it and prints `No models matching "<x>"` for an unknown
   one. Use it. Note `pi auth check --model <nonsense>` reports ready — it
   validates the PROVIDER only and is NOT a model oracle; do not reach for it.
   Decide and log where the check runs: compile time is where a bad tier should
   die, but the catalog is a live command, so state what happens when pi is
   absent (refuse, or degrade to the shape check and say so).

3. THE THINKING DIMENSION IS PER-MODEL. The catalog's `thinking` column is
   yes/no per model, and pi's effort is appended as a SUFFIX (`model:high`)
   rather than a flag. Several cloudflare models are `no`. Appending a level to
   one of those is the same class of error opencode's row already refuses. Use
   the catalog column to decide, and follow that precedent: a tier that asks for
   an effort a model has no dimension for is a refusal naming the tier, the
   model and the column, not a silent drop.

The point of all three: a tier must mean the model it names, or refuse. A tier
that silently becomes something else is worse than no tier, because the run's
own provenance will attest to the model that was requested.
acceptance_criteria: The pi row carries a full-auto template round-tripped LIVE, with its verified flag set, and the kinds reference's pi section is written from the actual run: echoed argv, agent_session, resume confirmed after a C-c restart under a fresh agent name, integration state recorded. A pi worker dispatched for a real tick completes an unattended turn without stalling on a permission prompt, shown end to end. THE SUBSTITUTION QUESTION IS ANSWERED IN WRITING: a deliberately unknown model id was run against pi and the RESULT file records whether pi refuses, errors visibly, or silently falls back to a default as opencode does; if it can substitute, a read-back proves the model that ran is the model the tier named, and a mismatch is a refusal. A tier's model id is validated against pi's own catalog (pi --list-models) rather than a slash check, so a typo dies at compile time; what happens when pi is absent is a logged decision. A bare id naming no provider is refused. An effort level on a model whose catalog thinking column is 'no' is refused naming the tier, the model and the column, matching the opencode precedent that a missing effort dimension is a refusal and not a silent drop. Tests cover a good pi tier, a typo'd model, a bare unqualified id, and an effort on a non-thinking model. Every pane and workspace created during verification is cleaned up. go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
